reviewed_fields.method: Retains the local fourth-moment proof's separate volume and capacity-defect allowances through its actual-source and physical transport wrappers. This replaces the narrower 22/5 capacity slice by an affine capacity and feeds a revised exact endpoint certificate into the all-Dirichlet continuation argument. Builds on nielstron's local 22/5 moment, Zhongpai Gao's local-moment work, Hailey Collet's Cycle25 framework, Akash Levy's weighted numerator, and OpenAI/math. Prepared with AI assistance.

Replaces the pointwise numerator bound in the cubic-theta probe of OpenAI's argument by a weighted fourth moment of the reflected physical numerator: Mellin inversion and the Hecke functional equation reduce the actual smoothed numerator sum to a plain polynomial of length at most U/Y, and the unused length carries selected prime factors in the original fourth moment, while a coefficient-norm argument controls the original Euler correction and its ramified error terms. The moment parameter stays at the original kappa = 3/4; with ell = 167/1000, theta = 11/12 - ell/4 = 10499/12000, and the finite exponent comparisons are exact rational certificates. Lean 4.34.1 development of 228 modules on the akashlevy/math fork (c388e88e6) of OpenAI/math fd4aeeb, with Mathlib d13f23b7; it proves zeta, all-Dirichlet and finite-order Hecke nonvanishing for Re s > 10499/12000.
Refinement of the OpenAI framework to 3499999/4000000. The pinned original proof has been independently reproduced and checked with Comparator and three kernels.

Absolute convergence of the Euler products gives nonvanishing of the Riemann zeta function and every Dirichlet L-function for Re(s) > 1. This is the classical starting bound; quasi-RH asks for a fixed boundary strictly below 1.

The exact boundary is 11/12−ℓ/4, where ℓ is the unique root in [1/6,1/5] of 927ℓ⁴−3135ℓ³+2433ℓ²+275ℓ−100=0. The plotted rational 683505193/781250000 is a proved upper bound less than 4×10⁻¹⁴ above it. The proof extends the unconditional common-mesh moving-radical moment and applies weighted low/high estimates and analytic continuation to Dirichlet, zeta and finite-order Eisenstein Hecke L-functions.

An unconditional all-Dirichlet zero-free half-plane at theta=874861/1000000, with strict boundary and the principal pole excluded. The proof combines earlier moment and physical-source estimates with Zhongpai Gao’s local refinement, extends the density range and local numerical region, and supplies a common probe for zero exclusion. It builds on OpenAI’s seven-eighths framework, Akash Levy’s weighted-numerator work, and the earlier AI-assisted QRH research directed by Hailey Collet. Hailey is the sole human author; research direction and source integration are distinguished from the AI-produced derivations, substantial drafting and formalization. Exact source attribution is retained in the paper and accompanying provenance.

Builds on Kari Roegnvaldsson, nielstron, OpenAI, Akash Levy, Hailey Collet, and Gao's earlier adapters. AI-assisted; inherited notices retained.

Coherent amplification and a joint reconstructed-row density estimate preserve cancellation through the error terms; independent heights, coefficient dilations and physical normalization feed the low/high assembly and unconditional continuation argument.

Builds on the complete Cycle61 construction and the listed predecessor proofs; inherited source attribution is preserved.
